_readme: Single content source for The Occult Archives. Edit this file, then upload it. Netlify runs scripts/build_archives.py on every deploy and regenerates the archive index pages, catalogue, related links and sitemap entries. See scripts/PUBLISHING-GUIDE.md.

dee.alt: Oil portrait of John Dee at sixty-seven: a long white beard, white ruff, black cap and fur-trimmed gown before a red curtain
dee.credit: Portrait of John Dee, unknown artist, c. 1594. Ashmolean Museum, Oxford. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

kelley.alt: Engraved portrait of Edward Kelley in a cap and fur-collared robe, holding an open book inscribed Trithemius, captioned Edw. Kelly, Prophet or Seer to Dr. Dee
kelley.credit: Edward Kelley, Alchemist, Friend of Dr. John Dee. Engraving, unknown artist. National Gallery of Art, Washington, Rosenwald Collection. Public domain.

prague.alt: Engraved view of Prague Castle and St. Vitus Cathedral above the Lesser Town, with walls and vineyards in the foreground
prague.credit: Prague Castle and the Lesser Town, after the 1607 view by Aegidius Sadeler, reproduced by Jaroslav Kosina, 1900. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

ring.alt: An ancient silver ring with an engraved scarab seal, shown beside its separated hoop and a dark impression of the seal
ring.label: Comparable period object, not the Ring of Solomon
ring.credit: Silver pendant ring with scarab, Phoenician, 9th to 8th century BCE. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Cesnola Collection (74.51.4170). Public domain.

temple.alt: Engraved plate showing a reconstruction of the Temple of Solomon from above, with the Ark and cherubim, the altar of incense, the Tabernacle and the figure of Moses
temple.label: Artistic reconstruction
temple.credit: The Temple of Solomon, its grounds and some of its interiors. Engraving. Wellcome Collection. Public Domain Mark.

walters.alt: Persian manuscript painting of King Solomon enthroned on a gold ground, surrounded by angels, demons, birds and beasts
walters.credit: King Solomon (Sulayman) enthroned, right side of a double-page frontispiece, Safavid Iran, 1539. Walters Art Museum, W.631. Creative Commons Zero.

grailproc.alt: Medieval manuscript painting in two panels: on the left, attendants carry a draped object; on the right, a maiden bears the Grail into a hall where crowned figures sit at a laid table
grailproc.credit: The Grail procession, from a manuscript of Chrétien de Troyes's Perceval and its continuations, Paris, c. 1330. Bibliothèque nationale de France, MS français 12577, f. 74v. Public domain.

percevalcastle.alt: Manuscript painting in two panels: a knight on a white horse arrives at a blue castle tower, and a feast is served at a table attended by maidens
percevalcastle.credit: Perceval arrives at the Grail Castle, French illuminated manuscript of the Perceval romances, 14th century. Public domain.

duncan.alt: Painting of pale, robed women at the edge of dark water; a hand rises from the lake holding a sword as a boat carries a wounded king
duncan.credit: John Duncan, The Taking of Excalibur, 1897. Public domain.

pyle.alt: Pen-and-ink drawing of a sword held upright from the water by a hand, radiating light, beside a crowned figure in a boat
pyle.credit: Howard Pyle, Excalibur the Sword, from The Story of King Arthur and His Knights, 1903. Public domain.

beardsley.alt: Black-and-white illustration within a floral border: the Lady of the Lake raises her hand to the armoured Arthur and the robed Merlin in a woodland
beardsley.credit: Aubrey Beardsley, The Lady of the Lake Telleth Arthur of the Sword Excalibur, from Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur (J. M. Dent edition), 1893–94. Public domain.

girflet.alt: Manuscript painting of a young man in a blue tunic and red hose standing at a lake shore, sword in hand, with a walled city behind
girflet.credit: Girflet at the lake with Excalibur, French illuminated manuscript of the Mort Artu, 15th century. In this French prose version the sword is returned by Girflet; in Malory it is Bedivere. Public domain.

draper.alt: Painting of Medea on the deck of the Argo, arm outstretched, as oarsmen strain and the golden fleece lies across the ship
draper.credit: Herbert James Draper, The Golden Fleece, 1904. Cartwright Hall Art Gallery, Bradford. Public domain.

boyvin.alt: Renaissance engraving within an ornate frame of figures and grotesques: Jason in armour confronts the dragon guarding the fleece
boyvin.credit: René Boyvin after Léonard Thiry, Jason confronting the dragon, from the Histoire de Jason, published 1563. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Public domain.

nolin.alt: Baroque engraving: an armoured Jason carries off the fleece between classical columns while putti fly overhead and the slain dragon lies at his feet
nolin.credit: Jean Nolin after Francesco Romanelli, Jason taking the Golden Fleece, 17th century engraving. Public domain.

reagans.alt: Formal portrait of Nancy Reagan in a red dress and Ronald Reagan in a dark suit, standing together beside red geraniums
reagans.credit: Ronald and Nancy Reagan, official White House portrait, 1980s. White House photograph, Ronald Reagan Presidential Library. Public domain.

reagansrain.alt: Nancy Reagan in a red suit and Ronald Reagan in a red cardigan, waving, as White House staff hold umbrellas over them in the rain
reagansrain.credit: The Reagans on the South Grounds of the White House, 1980s. White House photograph, Ronald Reagan Presidential Library. Public domain.

offeringseal.alt: Black stone cylinder seal beside its modern clay impression, showing robed figures in a presentation scene with columns of cuneiform inscription
offeringseal.credit: Mesopotamian cylinder seal and modern impression with a presentation scene and cuneiform inscription. Long before horoscopes, Mesopotamian scribes recorded the heavens as omens for kings. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access. Public domain.

ishtarseal.alt: Translucent stone cylinder seal beside its modern impression: a kneeling worshipper before a star-crowned goddess, flanked by winged figures
ishtarseal.credit: Neo-Assyrian cylinder seal and modern impression: a worshipper before a goddess encircled by stars, usually identified as Ishtar, the great goddess of Babylon and Assyria. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access. Public domain.

parsons.alt: Black-and-white photograph of Jack Parsons in a belted overcoat, standing in rocky scrubland above a rocket motor casing lashed to poles
parsons.credit: Jack Parsons with a rocket motor casing, 1940s. Photograph from the NASA/JPL archives.

chessking.alt: Small carved ivory king seated on a throne, crowned and bearded, holding an orb, with a lion at his feet
chessking.credit: Chess piece in the form of a king, medieval Europe, ivory. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access. Public domain.

gamepiece.alt: Round ivory gaming piece carved in openwork with human figures and a leaping beast inside a ringed border
gamepiece.credit: Medieval ivory gaming piece carved with figures and a beast. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access. Public domain.

tawlboard.alt: Diagram of an eleven-by-eleven game board in orange and brown, with white defending pieces and a king in a cross at the centre and black attackers on each edge
tawlboard.credit: Modern reconstruction of a tawlbwrdd board, the medieval Welsh game of the tafl family. The Welsh lists do not say which game Gwenddoleu's board was made for; this shows the kind of board the treasure is often compared with. Wikimedia Commons.
tawlboard.label: Illustrative reconstruction

menorahdetail.alt: Close view of the seven-branched menorah carved in relief on the Arch of Titus, standing on a stepped, decorated base
menorahdetail.credit: The menorah on the spoils relief, Arch of Titus, Rome, after 81 CE. Photograph via Wikimedia Commons.

titusfrieze.alt: Weathered marble relief of Roman soldiers carrying the great seven-branched menorah in procession
titusfrieze.credit: The spoils of Jerusalem carried in triumph, relief on the Arch of Titus, Rome, after 81 CE. Photograph via Wikimedia Commons.

gygeswoodcut.alt: Sixteenth-century woodcut labelled GYGES: a shepherd kneels and draws a ring from a hand reaching out of a door in the side of a fallen bronze horse
gygeswoodcut.credit: Gyges finds the ring in a bronze horse, 16th-century woodcut. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-1874-11-138-1. Public domain.

gygesferrara.alt: Renaissance painting: a shepherd ducks into the side of a golden horse while shepherds, women and sheep look on and a bearded god pours rain from a cloud
gygesferrara.credit: The story of the Ring of Gyges, Ferrarese school, 16th century. Public domain.

cagliostro.alt: Eighteenth-century engraved portrait of Cagliostro in a circular frame, looking upward, in an open-collared shirt and fur-trimmed coat
cagliostro.credit: Count Alessandro di Cagliostro, eighteenth-century engraved portrait. Public domain (18th-century engraving).

lorenza.alt: Eighteenth-century engraved portrait of a woman in a lace cap within a circular frame
lorenza.credit: Lorenza Feliciani, Cagliostro's wife, eighteenth-century engraved portrait. Public domain (18th-century engraving).

necklace.alt: Engraving of an elaborate diamond necklace with festoons and long tasselled pendants
necklace.credit: The diamond necklace of Böhmer and Bassenge, eighteenth-century engraving. Public domain (18th-century engraving).

shahnameh-folio.alt: Persian manuscript painting with a figure in a dark pit at the center and attendants around it, framed by text panels
shahnameh-folio.credit: A folio from a Persian manuscript of Ferdowsi's Shahnameh. The figure in the pit recalls the episode in which Kay Khosrow finds the imprisoned Bizhan through the world-revealing cup. Public domain (historical manuscript); supplied as an open-access museum image.

astro-bowl.alt: Medieval Iranian ceramic bowl painted with a central figure surrounded by a ring of seated figures and planetary motifs
astro-bowl.credit: An Iranian ceramic bowl painted with courtly and astrological figures. Persian vessels could carry the image of the ordered heavens, as the cup of Jamshid was said to. Public domain (medieval object; open-access museum photograph).

hafez-cup.alt: Persian miniature of a gathering of figures around a poet holding a cup, with lines of text above
hafez-cup.credit: Hafez gazing into the cup of Jamshid, Persian miniature (low-resolution source). Public domain.

cagliostro-banner.alt: Eighteenth-century engraved portrait of Cagliostro in a circular frame, looking upward, in an open-collared shirt and fur-trimmed coat
cagliostro-banner.credit: Count Alessandro di Cagliostro, eighteenth-century engraved portrait. Public domain (18th-century engraving).

chronicles.title: When the Angels Demanded Their Wives
chronicles.subtitle: John Dee, Edward Kelley, and one of the most disturbing episodes in the history of ceremonial magic.
chronicles.seoTitle: John Dee & Edward Kelley: When Angels Demanded Their Wives
chronicles.metaDescription: In 1587, John Dee and Edward Kelley recorded an extraordinary angelic command to share their wives. Discover the disturbing history behind Enochian magic.
chronicles.excerpt: In 1587, one of England's most accomplished intellectuals received an extraordinary instruction from what he believed to be a heavenly messenger.
heroCaption: English mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher and ceremonial magician.
chronicles.theme: When spiritual communications conflict with human judgment.

studies.why: Dee owned and studied Agrippa; his angelic work rests on the Renaissance philosophy of correspondence.
Enochian magic is one of the currents that converge in modern ceremonial magic.

chronicles.title: The Astrologer in the White House
chronicles.subtitle: Nancy Reagan, Joan Quigley and the celestial calculations behind an American presidency.
chronicles.seoTitle: Nancy Reagan's Astrologer: The Secret Astrology of the White House
chronicles.metaDescription: Discover how Nancy Reagan consulted astrologer Joan Quigley to help determine the timing of presidential events during the Reagan administration.
chronicles.excerpt: For seven years, an astrologer in San Francisco secretly advised the First Lady on the timing of presidential activities. How did an ancient occult science find its way into the modern White House?
chronicles.theme: When esoteric knowledge enters the affairs of worldly power.
heroCaption: The First Lady consulted the San Francisco astrologer Joan Quigley from 1981 until the arrangement became public in 1988.

studies.why: Electional astrology, the choice of favorable times, is studied in Stage IV.
The philosophy that gives astrology its meaning: as above, so below.

chronicles.title: The Rocket Scientist Who Invoked a Goddess
chronicles.subtitle: Jack Parsons, Aleister Crowley, L. Ron Hubbard and the Babalon Working of 1946.
chronicles.seoTitle: Jack Parsons and the Babalon Working: The Rocket Scientist Who Invoked a Goddess
chronicles.metaDescription: Discover how rocket scientist Jack Parsons, L. Ron Hubbard and Marjorie Cameron attempted to manifest the goddess Babalon through ceremonial magic in 1946.
chronicles.excerpt: In 1946, a pioneer of American rocketry enlisted the future founder of Scientology in a series of magical operations intended to manifest a goddess. Even Aleister Crowley had reservations.
chronicles.theme: When magical experimentation encounters the problem of discernment.
heroCaption: Rocket propulsion pioneer, co-founder of Aerojet and member of the Agape Lodge of the Ordo Templi Orientis.

studies.why: Parsons worked within Crowley's Thelema, one of the modern ceremonial currents traced in Stage VII.

chronicles.title: The Magician Who Stood Trial Before the French Monarchy
chronicles.subtitle: Count Cagliostro, Egyptian Freemasonry and the Affair of the Diamond Necklace.
chronicles.seoTitle: Cagliostro, Egyptian Freemasonry and the Diamond Necklace Affair
chronicles.metaDescription: In 1785 the magician Count Cagliostro was imprisoned in the Bastille over the Diamond Necklace Affair. The story of his trial, his Egyptian Rite and his legacy.
chronicles.excerpt: In 1785, one of Europe's most celebrated magicians was imprisoned in the Bastille over a diamond necklace that the Queen of France had never purchased.
chronicles.theme: When reputation and evidence must be judged separately.
heroCaption: Alchemist, healer and founder of the Egyptian Rite of Freemasonry.

studies.why: Cagliostro's Egyptian Rite raises the first question of the curriculum: what initiation is for, and how symbol and allegory teach.
His promise of physical and spiritual regeneration drew on the alchemical and Rosicrucian currents studied in Stage VI.
